name: GPT-Realtime Mini

voice.input_audio: PCM 16-bit mono at 24 kHz, G.711 mu-law or G.711 A-law over WebSocket and SIP, set in audio.input.format; WebRTC carries audio on media tracks; text and image items are also accepted [openai-ref-client-secrets] [openai-guide-conversations]
voice.output_audio: The same three formats, set in audio.output.format; WebRTC returns a remote audio track; a speed multiplier from 0.25 to 1.5 applies as post-processing [openai-ref-client-secrets] [openai-guide-conversations]
voice.voices: 10 built-in voices (alloy, ash, ballad, coral, echo, sage, shimmer, verse, marin, cedar), with marin and cedar recommended; custom voices for approved customers [openai-guide-conversations] [openai-guide-custom-voices]
voice.turn_detection: Server VAD (silence-based: threshold 0.5, prefix_padding_ms 300, silence_duration_ms 500 by default, optional idle_timeout_ms) or semantic VAD (eagerness low, medium, high or auto, with maximum waits of 8 s, 4 s and 2 s); on by default; create_response and interrupt_response can each be set to false; turn_detection null gives push-to-talk with manual commit and response.create [openai-guide-vad] [openai-ref-client-secrets]
voice.interruption: Yes. With VAD on, the start of user speech cancels the response in progress. On WebRTC and SIP the server drops unplayed audio from the conversation; on WebSocket the client stops playback and sends conversation.item.truncate [openai-guide-conversations]
voice.latency: Artificial Analysis time to first audio on Big Bench Audio: 0.8 s for the entry it labels October 2025 [aa-speech-to-speech]

pricing_usd_per_mtok.notes: numbers are audio-token rates; text $0.6 in, $0.06 cached, $2.4 out; image $0.8 in, $0.08 cached; Realtime endpoint only
